questions.q: What surprised researchers who tested the English national table tennis team's reactions?
a: The best player had the slowest reaction times
Every player reacted at exactly the same speed
The weakest player had the fastest reflexes
Reaction speed did not change with practice
questions.why: Lesson 1 describes Desmond Douglas, the best player, testing with the slowest reactions because his trained brain reads match situations quickly.

questions.q: According to the summary, which two changes does intensive practice create in the brain?
a: Faster situation reading and more subconscious control
A larger prefrontal cortex and quicker reflexes
Better memory and stronger willpower
Slower decisions and more conscious caution
questions.why: Lesson 1 says practice lets the brain assess complex game situations quickly and shifts execution to subconscious areas, freeing the prefrontal cortex.

questions.q: What does the summary mean by motivation by association?
a: A resemblance to a successful person pushes you to work harder
Training alongside experts automatically transfers their skill
Watching a sport regularly improves your own performance
Success spreads when people share the same coach
questions.why: Lesson 2 explains that finding even a slight similarity between yourself and someone successful can multiply your effort.

questions.q: What does the four-minute mile story illustrate in the summary?
a: One relatable record breaker can unlock belief in many others
Human bodies have a fixed limit on running speed
Records improve only through new running shoes
British runners are naturally faster than others
questions.why: Lesson 2 shows that after Roger Bannister broke the barrier, many runners with a link to Britain quickly followed.

questions.q: What technique does the summary suggest for avoiding a choke under pressure?
a: Telling yourself the event is not a big deal
Rehearsing every movement consciously
Focusing harder on what the crowd expects
Slowing your breathing before you begin
questions.why: Lesson 3 recommends reminding yourself the event does not really matter, which lets the subconscious apply your trained skills.
